title: Declarative EKS control-plane lifecycle Terraform module with staged upgrade blueprints and health sentinels
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a reusable Terraform module that provisions and manages the Redwood Private (VPC) EKS control plane and associated lifecycle guardrails. The module should enable declarative upgrades (planned rollouts), provide built-in health sentinels for pre/post-upgrade validation, and expose knobs for canary/blue-green upgrade strategies. This ticket covers the module API, implementation plan, automated health probes, and CI canary pipeline integration.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Module can create an EKS control plane and required networking resources in an isolated VPC using provided inputs.
2) Module exposes a 'lifecycle_blueprint' variable to select 'canary', 'staged', or 'immediate' upgrade strategies.
3) Upgrades can be executed with a dry-run flag that runs health sentinels without applying changes.
4) Health sentinels report pass/fail to an S3 artifact and optional Datadog event.
5) Canary rollouts support percentage-based control-plane node replacement and automatic rollback on sentinel failure.
6) Module is covered by unit tests and a full e2e pipeline that performs an upgrade in a disposable account/cluster.
design_notes: We will split responsibilities: Terraform will manage infrastructure and high-level lifecycle policy objects; a small bootstrap controller (Helm chart) will be deployed to the cluster to execute sentinel checks and coordinate node drain/cordon via the Kubernetes API. The controller will be optional for air-gapped customers; in that case the module will produce artifacts and manual runbooks. The module will support tagging, IAM roles with least privilege, and KMS-wrapped secrets for any bootstrap resources.
terraform_interface:
Inputs: cluster_name, vpc_id, subnet_ids, control_plane_instance_types, admin_roles, kms_key_arn, lifecycle_blueprint, canary_percentage, dry_run, upgrade_window, tags.
Outputs: eks_cluster_id, kubeconfig_blob (encrypted), lifecycle_plan_id, sentinel_artifact_bucket, last_upgrade_status.
Module versioning: follow semantic versioning; maintain migration notes for any breaking changes in module inputs.
upgrade_strategy:
Blueprints: 'canary' (replace X% of control-plane nodes and validate), 'staged' (roll sequential AZ-by-AZ with pause windows), 'immediate' (full replace).
Upgrade execution: Terraform applies will create a lifecycle_plan resource and set desired state. An orchestration step (CI job or cluster bootstrap controller) will read the plan and perform the in-cluster operations. If sentinels fail, orchestration will attempt an automatic rollback to the previous control-plane AMI/config and mark the plan failed.
health_checks: Built-in sentinels include: API server readiness (control plane endpoints), kube-apiserver latency sample, kube-scheduler and controller-manager process health (via metrics), simple control-plane API CRUD for a test namespace (create/read/delete pod), and integration smoke tests for token issuance with issuer. Sentinels run pre-upgrade (baseline), during-canary (post replace), and post-upgrade (stability window). Results are uploaded to sentinel_artifact_bucket as JSON and an aggregate status is emitted to Datadog and a Slack channel.
testing_plan: Local unit tests for Terraform using kitchen-terraform and terratest where possible. End-to-end tests run in CI against an ephemeral account: provision module, run baseline sentinels, trigger a canary upgrade, validate automated rollback on injected failure, and run post-upgrade stability checks for 30m. Add a synthetic load generator for a subset of tests to ensure KV cache / request routing behavior is unaffected by control-plane changes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): internal-only deploys in disposable accounts and manual validation by infra eng. Phase 2 (beta): integrate with CI pipeline and enable automatic sentinels; run scheduled canaries in staging. Phase 3 (GA): enable customer-facing upgrade pipeline, add RBAC controls, document runbooks and incident playbooks. Communication: announce in #infra and send release notes to Customer Success for any tenant-impacting changes.
risks:
- Automatic control-plane mutations are high-risk; incorrect IAM or tagging could orphan resources.
- Air-gapped customers may not allow bootstrap controller; require robust manual fallback steps.
- Sentinel false positives could cause unnecessary rollbacks; must tune thresholds.
- Terraform state drift during in-cluster operations if orchestration is not idempotent.
